extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of folklore/comparative mythology; general readers interested in cultural myths
extracted.subtask_description: A comparative compilation and discussion of lunar myths (man, woman, hare, toad, etc.) from many cultures, illustrating variations, sources, and interpretations. The text surveys traditions and offers interpretive commentary for a general or scholarly readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of religion as tasteful seasoning in entertainments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure religion is an Attic salt, which wise men use in all of their entertainments: a condiment which seasons what is otherwise insipid, and assists healthy digestion in the compound organism of man's mental and moral constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religion (or moral/religious content) should be used sparingly and skillfully in entertainments — as a seasoning that improves otherwise bland material and aids audience reception. It is presented here as a positive device for writers/entertainers to employ judiciously; the author introduces a lunar-journey tract that used religious teaching to move its lunar inhabitants, praising its moral purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary digressions; keep material relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: We must not be detained with any detailed account of M. Jules Verne's captivating books... They are accessible to all, at a trifling cost. Besides, they reveal nothing new relating to the Hamlet of our present play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling or discussing related works, omit lengthy summaries of tangential or well-known texts that do not contribute new insight to the primary subject. Prioritize relevance and brevity in comparative or critical surveys to maintain focus on the main topic.
